newsitem.title: UK: Cedel launches OTC derivative risk-management tool.
newsitem.headline: Cedel launches OTC derivative risk-management tool.

text.p: Cedel Bank said it was launching a new risk-management system on Monday which could improve the safety of trading over-the-counter (OTC) derivatives, a market estimated to be worth up to $50 trillion.
"Regulators will be pleased to see this development, which tackles the risk involved in trading derivatives," said Gerald Sampson, head of the new product at Cedel Bank.
Cedel Bank said its global credit support service (GCSS), operational from Monday, was the first ever real-time book-entry service for management of collateral in the derivatives market.
GCSS was the result of an 18-month effort involving eight players in the OTC derivatives market, Cedel Bank said.

"At a time when collateralisation as a means of controlling credit exposures is steadily rising, GCSS establishes a new standard for the management of credit support assets to minimise risk in the trading of derivatives," it said in a statement.

"Collateralisation is steadily growing as financial institutions respond to the Capital Adequacy Directive and Basle Committee guidelines. GCSS offers the ability to maximise asset efficiency and lower collateral funding costs," Cedel said.

A large part of the OTC derivatives market consists of swaps, but other instruments like options are also traded. To cover the risk of a counterparty defaulting on a derivatives contract, players require high-quality assets as collateral.

GCSS will kick off with four customers -- Bank of America, Banque Paribas, Dresdner Bank and Salomon Brothers -- and Cedel Bank said several other firms had signed letters of intent. Sampson said OTC derivatives players had a number of needs, many of which were provided by the new system.

These included full customisation of credit support agreement terms, 24-hour real-time collateralisation, optimisation of asset usage, re-using the same collateral for different securities, seamless cross-currency substitution, elimination of legal uncertainty and no limit on the products that it could be used with.

"(GCSS) has been designed to be efficient and cost effective and the consequent reduction of potential systemic risk through using this technology will be welcomed generally by regulators," said Cris Larson, senior vice president at Bank of America Global Capital Markets Group in San Francisco.

Also commenting on the system, Augustine Vargetto, vice president at Salomon Brothers, said: "GCSS offers cost benefits to our front, middle and back offices. A real-time global system, it allows us to make maximum use of our collateral, regardless of time zone constraints".
